nodes.name: Smooth cordgrass
nodes.desc: Dominant grass of the seaward salt marsh. It traps sediment and builds the marsh edge, and snow geese dig up its rhizomes.

nodes.name: Common reed
nodes.desc: Tall reed that forms dense stands in brackish and freshwater marsh. Muskrats and ducks use it for food and cover.

nodes.name: Diatoms and dinoflagellates
nodes.desc: Microscopic algae drifting in the bay and tidal creeks. They feed filter-feeders such as mussels.

nodes.name: Sweetgum
nodes.desc: Common hardwood of the refuge uplands and wooded swamp. Its seeds are eaten by squirrels and goldfinches.

nodes.name: Atlantic ribbed mussel
nodes.desc: Filter-feeding marsh bivalve that eats phytoplankton and bacteria. Birds, raccoons and blue crabs eat it.

nodes.name: Snow goose
nodes.desc: Winter visitor that gathers in huge flocks at the refuge. It pulls up cordgrass rhizomes in the marsh.

nodes.name: Muskrat
nodes.desc: Marsh rodent that eats reeds and other aquatic plants and builds lodges. Prey for foxes, raccoons and eagles.

nodes.name: Mallard
nodes.desc: Abundant dabbling duck on the managed pools and tidal creeks. It eats seeds and marsh plants.

nodes.name: Eastern gray squirrel
nodes.desc: Common in the refuge woods, where it eats seeds and nuts such as sweetgum fruit.

nodes.name: American horseshoe crab
nodes.desc: Spawns on Delaware Bay beaches in spring, females laying thousands of eggs. It eats molluscs and worms.

nodes.name: Red knot
nodes.desc: Long-distance shorebird that stops on the bay to feast on horseshoe crab eggs and nearly doubles its weight.

nodes.name: Laughing gull
nodes.desc: Abundant coastal gull that joins shorebirds in feeding on horseshoe crab eggs on the beaches.

nodes.name: Raccoon
nodes.desc: Omnivore of marsh and woods. It eats muskrats, ducks, squirrels and ribbed mussels.

nodes.name: Turkey vulture
nodes.desc: Soaring scavenger that cleans up carcasses of mammals and birds across the refuge.

nodes.name: Bald eagle
nodes.desc: Threatened species at the refuge that takes ducks, geese, gulls and muskrats.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: Common refuge predator that eats muskrats, ducks, squirrels and raccoons.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Drives growth of marsh grasses and plankton in the shallow bay.

nodes.name: Tides
nodes.desc: Spring tides flood the marsh and let female horseshoe crabs spawn at the high-water line.

nodes.name: Marsh mud & nutrients
nodes.desc: Tidal sediment holds the nutrients that marsh plants draw on.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Bacteria and fungi break down dead marsh grass and carcasses, returning nutrients to the mud.
